init.title: Cost tracking
init.description: Configure how energy cost is recorded alongside usage. Pick a meter to set its cost source, then choose Save to apply.

data_description.meter: Choose a meter to configure, or Save and apply to finish.

meter.title: Cost source
meter.description:
Set the cost source for {meter}.

- Entity: price from a `sensor`, `number`, or `input_number`. A sensor with long-term statistics (state class `measurement`) gives accurate per-hour historical cost; a `number`/`input_number` (or a stateless sensor) has no history, so it prices flat at its current value going forward — an easily editable rate you manage independently of this dialog (a backfill reprices all history at its current value).
- Static: a fixed rate in {unit} applied to every interval, changed only here.
- Off: no cost tracking (existing cost statistics are kept).

data_description.entity_id: Used when the cost source is Entity. Pick a sensor, number, or input_number holding the rate in {unit}.
data_description.price: Used when the cost source is Static. Enter the rate in {unit}.

data_description.backfill_cost: Enabling this reloads the integration and reprices all past usage for every configured meter (using the earliest/static price available). Leave it off for normal operation; it turns itself back off once the backfill completes.

error.no_price_data: The selected entity has neither long-term statistics nor a numeric current value, so it cannot price usage.
error.entity_required: Select a price entity, or choose a different cost source.
error.price_required: Enter a static price, or choose a different cost source.
error.invalid_price: The static price must be a positive number.
